messages:
courtney: Auditor (SOC2 fieldwork) asked for a compact runbook + artifacts proving ephemeral KMS keys used by task-executor are created, used, and destroyed, and that the RBAC change last sprint was logged. They want a 30-day window ending 2026-03-15. Can oncall assemble?

samir: I can pull Splunk and KMS metadata. Quick Q — do they want raw logs or aggregated counts + signed manifests?

courtney: Raw logs preferred, but they also asked for a signed manifest listing key_ids and operations (create/encrypt/decrypt/destroy). Minimal screenshots ok if we include hash of exported files.

maria: Checklist to hand over (short):
- Splunk export (CSV + MD5) for KMS events 2026-02-15 -> 2026-03-15
- Key manifest (JSON) with key_id, creation_ts, rotation_ts, owner, purpose; signed by infra lead
- RBAC diff from git between commit a1b2c3..d4e5f6 (service-account and rolebinding changes)
- SIEM correlation file (alert ids) and one sample audit playback (screencap)
- Short memo on vuln triage & mitigation for any KMS-related finding

alex: PR with RBAC change is here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1298 — includes rolebindings for task-executor and a short audit comment. Use `git show d4e5f6` for the diff.

samir: Splunk query I used (paste for reproducibility):
```splunk
index=infra kernel OR kms (action=Encrypt OR action=Decrypt OR action=CreateKey OR action=DestroyKey) resource="arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/*" earliest=02/15/2026:00:00:00 latest=03/15/2026:23:59:59
| table _time, host, user, action, key_id, request_id, src_ip
| sort _time
```

samir: Example log snippet (sanitized):
"2026-03-10T14:12:03Z host=task-runner-03 user=svc-task-exec action=CreateKey key_id=key-0a1b2c request_id=req-89ab"

courtney: Auditor asked specifically for chain-of-custody proof for ephemeral keys (creation->usage->destroy). We should include KMS key version IDs and any envelope-id used by the runtime.

maria: For the manifest please include fields: key_id, key_version, created_by, created_ts, deleted_ts (if any), linked_pod/task_id, signed_by. I can sign the manifest once we assemble.

samir: FYI during triage we saw a KMS plugin misbind that allowed a stale role to be accepted briefly — tracked it as a vuln and patched on 2026-03-10. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kms-plugin/pull/212. No evidence of exfil, but we must include the vulnerability memo.

alex: Triage summary to add for auditor:
- Finding: role-binding mismatch allowed stale token acceptance for ~13 minutes (2026-03-10T14:00-14:13)
- Impact: limited to ephemeral task-executor tokens; no cross-tenant access
- Fix: validation tightened + added replay-protection; rolled 3 replicas, mitigation verified
- Evidence: deployment logs, post-fix CI run (artifact hash), before/after config diff

auditor_bot: Please include a signed SHA256 hash of all exported files and an exported SIEM correlation id list. If possible, attach a timestamped attestation (e.g., SLSA-style) stating files are unmodified.

maria: I'll produce the manifest and sign it. Samir — can you export Splunk to CSV and put the export in `s3://redwood-audit-temp/5771234567/` with MD5 and SHA256 sidecars? Then post the pre-signed URL to this thread.

samir: On it. Exporting now (estimate 10–15m). Using export name `kms_events_20260215_20260315.csv.gz` — MD5: `b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184` (placeholder), SHA256: `e3b0c44298fc1c149afb` (will replace).

courtney: Also attach the `aws kms get-key-rotation-status` output and a `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key>` sample for at least two key_ids to show permissions. Example command I ran: `aws kms list-keys --region us-east-1`

maria: For RBAC diff, I'll export `git diff --staged a1b2c3 d4e5f6 > rbac_change.diff` and include author emails + commit SHAs.

samir: Done with export and uploaded to s3; posted pre-signed URL to the auditor Slack DM. (link redacted) :thumbsup:

courtney: Auditor replied — they want the signed manifest + replay of one sample request (we should produce a playback using logs + signed hash). They also asked whether ephemeral keys are rotated automatically and whether rotation metadata is logged.

maria: Answer for auditor: ephemeral key lifecycle: created on-demand by task-executor, bound to task_id, rotated (destroy/create) on task termination unless retention policy applies. Rotation events are logged (CreateKey/DestroyKey) and we also log envelope_id and linked task_id. I'll include the retention policy snippet.

alex: One more note — for ISO controls they asked about retention and hashing of logs. We keep raw logs 90 days in S3 (WORM for audit exports) and indexed data in Splunk for 365 days. We'll include the retention policy link and the S3 bucket policy screenshot.

samir: Also flagged: we should backfill any missing rotation events during the vulnerability window — I'll cross-check KMS cloudtrail for gaps and annotate the evidence package if we had to reconstruct events.

courtney: Great. Plan: samir finishes logs + hashes, maria produces signed manifest and RBAC diff, alex bundles PR links + deployment logs, I will draft the short memo for the auditor describing the vuln triage and remediation timeline. Aim to deliver final ZIP by EOD.

maria: Will sign the manifest and upload. If auditor requests notarized timestamp, we can use our timestamping service.

auditor_bot: Received preliminary package, will schedule fieldwork review call tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Please be ready to walk through the evidence.

courtney: Thanks all — ping me here when uploads are complete and I'll move to final bundle. :handshake:
